summary: Dar es Salaam is one of East Africa's most livable cities for diaspora professionals, with well-established expat zones on the Msasani Peninsula and Oyster Bay that rank among the safest in the region. Petty theft and phone snatching are the primary concerns in market and CBD areas. Standard precautions in the main expat zones keep risk manageable. A background terrorism threat exists primarily for coastal areas and Zanzibar.
dataSource: US State Dept, UK FCO, Numbeo 2025, OSAC

usDeptState.label: Exercise Increased Caution
usDeptState.summary: Exercise increased caution due to crime and terrorism. Petty theft, purse snatching, and pick-pocketing are common, especially in Dar es Salaam.

ukFco.summary: Tanzania has a generally lower crime rate than other countries in the region. Take reasonable precautions. Some areas of Dar have higher rates of street crime.

crimeTypes: Phone grabbing from hands and open car windows
currentAlerts: Terrorism risk persists in coastal areas and Zanzibar. Occasional bomb threats in Dar es Salaam proper.
May 2025: Advisory updated with elevated terrorism threat for Western interests.
Zanzibar has a distinct and somewhat elevated risk profile from Dar es Salaam city.
Tourist areas are specifically targeted by opportunistic crime.
safetyTips: Never display your phone or camera in Kariakoo or any market area.
Avoid walking along the Masaki-Oyster Bay beachfront after dark.
Use Bolt or verified app taxis only. Street taxis carry robbery risk.
Swim only at designated and staffed beaches. Strong rip currents and isolated beach muggings occur.
Keep vehicle doors locked and windows up in traffic.
Do not carry large cash amounts. Use ATMs inside secured banks or malls.
To report a crime or call police, dial 112. For medical emergencies dial 114. For fire dial 115. These are the national emergency lines for Tanzania.

US citizens contact the U.S. Embassy Dar es Salaam at +255 22 229 4000 for emergency consular assistance. UK nationals contact the British High Commission at +255 22 229 0000. Both offer 24-hour emergency lines for citizens in distress.
Enroll in the US Embassy Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) at step.state.gov to receive real-time security alerts for Tanzania.

keyFacts: Tanzania has a good regional safety record. Msasani Peninsula and Oyster Bay are among the safest expat zones in East Africa.
Terrorism is a background risk, primarily affecting Zanzibar and coastal areas, not central Dar es Salaam.
English and Swahili are both widely spoken, aiding communication with authorities.
Dar es Salaam offers a significantly more affordable lifestyle than comparable East African cities.
highlights: Safe expat zones well-established with good security infrastructure
One of East Africa's most livable cities for diaspora professionals
English widely spoken, easier to navigate for diaspora

challenges: Phone snatching epidemic in market and CBD areas
